subject: Request: temporary throttle lift for Crestline onboarding
messages:
From: Anna Dawes <anna.dawes@crestline.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@crestline.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding spike — temporary throttle increase request

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from the ops team: during our staging-to-prod rollout this week we're seeing sustained traffic spikes as we warm caches and run automated evals. Our initial tests will push ~4x the baseline RPS for a 6–8 hour window on Sunday (Mar 7).

Given Crestline is committing to a 12-month Dedicated plan once onboarding completes, can Redwood provision a temporary throttle lift (burst quota) for that window so the rollout tests complete without repeated 429s? We understand fairness policies; we can sign any temporary addendum and agree to guardrails.

Appreciate a quick yes/no and what info you need from procurement.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Dawes
Head of Platform Engineering — Crestline Health
Attachments: Crestline_Onboarding_Specs.xlsx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Dawes <anna.dawes@crestline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding spike — temporary throttle increase request

Hi Anna — thanks for the heads up and the spec sheet.

Short answer: yes, we can support a time‑boxed uplift, but we need to coordinate the governance steps and technical constraints:
- Proposed approach: a 6‑hour burst window with a soft ceiling 4x baseline and automatic ramp‑down.
- Controls: per‑token accounting, request provenance headers, and an enforced concurrency cap to protect other shared tenants.
- SLA impact: raising the burst quota does not change uptime SLAs, but it does relax our fairness throttles temporarily. Any customer‑facing SLA credits would still follow standard incident/process.

Next steps for procurement: please have Crestline procurement sign the temporary addendum and return the MSA redlines. If you can provide a primary contact for DocuSign, we can pre-fill the addendum and a short mutual action plan (MAP).

Ben — can you confirm the runtime limits and whether a quantized model variant could reduce token pressure for this burst? Marissa / Monica — tagging for legal/procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Anna Dawes <anna.dawes@crestline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding spike — temporary throttle increase request

Anna — quick technical follow up.

We ran the spec you sent through our capacity planner. Two options to keep latency within your target while lowering token cost:
1) Temporary model variant (quantized, lower context) for noisy, high‑frequency evaluation traffic. Reduces per‑token GPU time ~35% but may change subtle response distribution.
2) Maintain full model but route evaluation traffic to a dedicated burst pool with a 6‑hour reservation; this preserves fidelity but consumes reserved ops.

For fairness we will:
- Apply a tagged burst label on requests to mark the window
- Limit total shared capacity impact by capping concurrency and enabling preemptible lower‑priority workers after 80% utilization

I attached a short carveout wording (Provisional_Rate_Carveout_2027-03-02.docx) and a small sample config. If Crestline prefers minimal fidelity divergence, choose option 2. If cost is the concern, option 1 is viable for staged tests.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Provisional_Rate_Carveout_2027-03-02.docx
From: procurement@crestline.com
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Dawes <anna.dawes@crestline.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@crestline.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Onboarding spike — temporary throttle increase request

Karthik — procurement here. We can expedite the addendum but need two items before sign:
1) A clear liability stub confirming temporary lift does not change data residency or retention terms.
2) A DocuSign link for the addendum and a short MAP listing the exact UTC window and rollback criteria.

We have one question on billing: will the uplift be invoiced as an overage (per‑token) or as a one‑time provisional fee? Crestline prefers predictable one‑time billing for the test window.

Please provide the drafted addendum and the billing option you recommend; we'll try to return a signed copy within 24 hours.

Procurement Team
Crestline Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@crestline.com
Cc: Anna Dawes <anna.dawes@crestline.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding spike — temporary throttle increase request

Thanks — attaching the DocuSign prefill and our recommended terms inline:
- Window: 2027-03-07T02:00:00Z to 2027-03-07T10:00:00Z (UTC).
- Billing: one‑time provisional fee equal to estimated extra compute; final reconciliation against actual per‑token usage with a cap at 125% of estimate.
- Liability/data: temporary lift does not alter data residency/retention; all requests remain subject to existing MSA.
- Rollback criteria: we will auto‑terminate the burst if shared tenant latency degradation > 30% or error rate > 2% for a 10‑minute window.

If procurement signs the addendum in DocuSign (link: https://docusign.example.com/crestline-addendum-CRST-2027-042) we will schedule the provisional reservation and ship the routing tag.

Marissa — legal has been looped for final signoff. Monica — please add this carveout to the deal record and set the HubSpot task to trigger a post‑burst cost reconciliation.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Crestline_MSA_Draft.pdf
